abstract: REcTO4 (R4) is an engineered chimeric protein that combines the PIN endoribonuclease domain of Regnase-1 with the tandem zinc-finger (TZF) RNA-binding domain of tristetraprolin (TTP), designed to promote the targeted degradation of pro-inflammatory mRNAs. Recombinant production and purification of this bifunctional chimeric protein in soluble form presents substantial challenges, including the need to accommodate two structurally distinct functional domains that must fold in the bacterial cytoplasm, as well as the interaction of the TZF domain with endogenous RNA. Here, we describe the systematic expression, screening, optimization of purification procedures, and biochemical/biophysical characterization of recombinant GST-tagged R4. Among the five expression constructs designed, only the N-terminally GST-tagged construct yielded an appreciable amount of soluble, catalytically active protein in Escherichia coli. An optimized two-step purification protocol, combining GST affinity and size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), yielded GST-R4 with a purity exceeding 95%. GST-R4 also co-purifies with endogenous bacterial RNA, forming high-molecular-weight complexes with apparent molecular mass of approximately 570 kDa by SEC. Endoribonuclease assay performed after affinity purification showed detectable RNA-cleavage activity. Preliminary cryo-EM micrographs reveal heterogeneous particles of approximately 10 nm, together with filamentous features consistent with assemblies of RNA-protein complexes, but intrinsic sample heterogeneity currently prevents 2D/3D reconstruction. This methodology reported here establishes an expression and purification workflow for GST-R4 and provides a foundation for structural and functional studies of this novel chimeric enzyme class engineered for pharmacological application.
